intervals.label: 6-detector configuration
intervals.note: Dates from the final Daya Bay oscillation paper (arXiv:2211.14988), which lists the six-, eight- and seven-detector running periods.
intervals.quote: From 24 December 2011 to 28 July 2012 (217 days), the experiment ran in an initial six-AD configuration with 2 ADs in EH1, 1 AD in EH2 and 3 ADs in EH3

intervals.label: 8-detector configuration
intervals.note: Dates from the final Daya Bay oscillation paper (arXiv:2211.14988). Earlier text had this interval ending in 2020 (Wikipedia operating period), but the eight-detector configuration ended on 20 December 2016; seven detectors ran from 26 January 2017 (next interval).
intervals.quote: An AD was added to both EH2 and EH3 during the summer of 2012 and this eight-AD configuration was operated from 19 October 2012 until 20 December 2016 (1524 days).

intervals.label: 7-detector configuration
intervals.note: Dates from the final Daya Bay oscillation paper (arXiv:2211.14988). 12 December 2020 is the end of the data set used in that paper.
intervals.quote: Seven-AD operation occurred from 26 January 2017 until 12 December 2020 (1417 days) with one AD in EH1 re-purposed for liquid scintillator R&D for the JUNO experiment

intervals.label: shut down
intervals.note: Year taken from the end of data taking on 12 December 2020 (final Daya Bay oscillation paper); that source does not state the date the detectors were physically shut down.
intervals.quote: Seven-AD operation occurred from 26 January 2017 until 12 December 2020 (1417 days) with one AD in EH1 re-purposed for liquid scintillator R&D for the JUNO experiment

name: Daya Bay antineutrino detectors
notes: Modelled as a single detector-system record covering all (six, later eight) functionally identical antineutrino detectors, per the detector paper's own description of them as 'functionally identical'; individual AD1-AD8 unit records are not in the Atlas.

placements.note: Daya Bay near hall (470 m flux-weighted baseline). Placed at the shared campus-grade site point (see site note); hall-specific coordinates not found.
placements.quote: two near (flux-weighted baseline 470 m and 576 m) and one far (1648 m) underground experimental halls

placements.note: Ling Ao near hall (576 m flux-weighted baseline). Placed at the shared campus-grade site point (see site note); hall-specific coordinates not found.
placements.quote: two near (flux-weighted baseline 470 m and 576 m) and one far (1648 m) underground experimental halls

placements.note: Far hall (1648 m baseline). Placed at the shared campus-grade site point (see site note); hall-specific coordinates not found.
placements.quote: two near (flux-weighted baseline 470 m and 576 m) and one far (1648 m) underground experimental halls

target_mass.display: 20 t Gd-doped liquid scintillator per detector
target_mass.note: Target (gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator) mass per antineutrino detector; the final Daya Bay paper (arXiv:2211.14988) gives 20 tonnes of GdLS in each AD.
target_mass.quote: Each AD consists of a Stainless Steel Vessel (SSV) containing 3 detector zones filled with different liquids ... The innermost target zone contains 20 tons of gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator (GdLS) inside an Inner Acrylic Vessel (IAV).

summary.plain: A set of identical tank-like detectors, each holding 20 tonnes of a liquid that glows when antineutrinos interact in it, spread across near and far halls at Daya Bay.
summary.technical: Six (2011-2012), then eight (2012-2016), then seven (2017-2020) functionally identical Gd-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors, each ~20 t target mass, deployed across the Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near and far underground halls.

technology.value: Functionally identical cylindrical antineutrino detectors filled with gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator, viewed by photomultiplier tubes
